camps.name: Luna Camp, Big Beaver Trail
camps.why: Flat old-growth camp on the Big Beaver trail, the first night after the boat and the easy last night before the walk out; it spares a long bushwhack day at each end.

camps.name: Luna Cirque floor
camps.why: The bowl under the glacier: running water, shelter on three sides and the shortest way to the climb. Parties that stay put sleep here through the summit days.

plan_conflict: The plan adds a separate advance camp below the icefall on nights 3 and 4, but no site is on file and no party was found using one; nights 3-5 follow the plan's shape, only nights 1-2 are backed by a party that slept at Luna Camp then at the head of Access Creek.

camps.name: Whatcom Camp, Brush Creek below Whatcom Pass
camps.why: Last trail camp below the pass, in trees beside Brush Creek; it makes the glacier crossing the whole of day 2. Check that it is open, since fire damage has closed sites here.

camps.name: Crooked Thumb Glacier moraine high camp
camps.why: The camp nearest Phantom: the summit day is a round trip from the moraine. Water is meltwater, and two glacier crossings stand between it and the pass.

camps.name: Perfect Pass, Perfect Pass cross-country zone
camps.why: Benches on the way past the Challenger Glacier; stop here instead of at the pass camp to shorten day 2, though day 1 grows by several miles.

camps.name: Luna Cirque floor
camps.why: Belongs to the Ross Lake side of the Pickets; a party coming over Whatcom Pass does not sleep here.

camps.name: Luna Camp, Big Beaver Trail
camps.why: Trail camp on Big Beaver, on the Ross Lake approach; it is not on the Hannegan Pass plan.

plan_conflict: Camps on file list Luna Cirque floor as a main camp, but the Hannegan Pass plan never sleeps there; Whatcom Camp is used for nights 1 and 4 by plan shape, and the plan itself says it may be closed.

camps.name: Luna Camp, Big Beaver Trail
camps.why: First night of the Ross Lake approach: flat, forested and close to the start of the Access Creek bushwhack, so day 2 starts fresh.

camps.name: Luna Col bivy, Luna cross-country zone
camps.why: High bivy above the cirque on rock, heather or snow; no built sites, but snow for water and the Fury traverse begins right from it.

camps.name: Luna Cirque floor
camps.why: Lower option on the traverse that skips the col; it adds a descent and a climb back up, so most parties push on to the col.

new_camps.name: Glacier col bivy past West Fury
new_camps.why: Where the Fury traverse ends: a wind-scoured snow hollow in the col before Swiss. No real site, but it saves carrying on in the dark after the rappels.
new_camps.notes: A bivy on the climb itself, found on snow; no tent platforms, no ground water. It is a bivy on the route so no elevation is given.

plan_conflict: The plan gives no camps for days 3 and 4; night 3 comes from a single traverse party, and day 1 names both Luna Camp and Access Creek.

new_camps.name: Easy Peak bivy
new_camps.why: Where day 1 ends on the crest; a tarn sits close by, and it leaves the Impasse and Perfect Pass for the next morning.
new_camps.notes: Elevation is the app's own pin. Other parties have slept on the ridge lower down.

new_camps.name: Perfect Pass
new_camps.why: The nearest camp to the south buttress, about 45 minutes from its base; sleep here after the climb rather than walk out the same evening.
new_camps.notes: Elevation reported between about 6,240 and 6,300 ft. Windy, and snow-covered early in the season.

plan_conflict: The plan hikes all the way out on day 3, so night 2 at Perfect Pass is an assumption; no account of a party's nights on this route was found.

camps.name: Easy Ridge bivouac ground below Easy Peak
camps.why: Ends day 1 high on the crest with tarn water near the top of the climbers' path, before the Impasse bypass the next morning.

camps.name: Perfect Pass, Perfect Pass cross-country zone
camps.why: Benches below the south face; the plan reaches them before the climb and leaves them after, so it is the night spot for the summit day.

camps.name: Whatcom Camp, Brush Creek below Whatcom Pass
camps.why: Sits on the walk out; tired parties may stop here after the summit rather than continue down toward the Chilliwack River.

plan_conflict: The plan sleeps night 3 at US Cabin Camp, which is not on file and for which no elevation could be found, so night 3 has no main camp here; no party following this plan was found.

camps.name: Terror Basin camp
camps.why: The one mountain camp for the spire: flat, with running water nearby, and the summit day starts and ends here. It fills up on busy weekends, and a permit is needed.

camps.name: Goodell Creek Campground, roadhead staging
camps.why: Car camping the night before for a first-light start up the steep approach; it adds nothing to the mountain days.

camps.name: Old Goodell Creek roadbed near the Terror Creek crossing
camps.why: A flat spot on the way in if you stop early; the climb to the basin is steep and long, so most parties push through to the basin.

camps.name: Cutthroat Lake basin, outside the quarter-mile closure
camps.why: Closest legal camp below the peak, but low on the approach and limited by closure rules; expect a longer climbing day than from a camp in the upper basin.

camps.name: Cutthroat Creek trailhead
camps.why: A night at the car before the walk in; it adds no height, and the approach is the same length the next morning.

plan_conflict: Camps on file list the trailhead as main, but the plan's night is spent at the end of the approach; no party's sleeping place on this route was found.

camps.name: Upper Diobsud Lakes
camps.why: The plan's traverse ends here: lake water and flat benches, and the summit is a round trip from camp the next day.

camps.name: Anderson Creek road end, Watson Lakes trailhead
camps.why: The road end only; sleep here for an early start, not as a camp for the trip.

camps.name: Lower Anderson Lake
camps.why: Sits right under the climbers' ridge path, so it suits a late start; the plan walks past it on day 1.

camps.name: Watson Lakes designated camps
camps.why: A short walk from the road with lake water and the best sites nearby; stop here if starting late, then do the traverse next morning.

camps.name: Northeast Bacon camp, above the glacier
camps.why: A higher camp near the summit for a quicker push or carrying over after the climb; it can be dry late in summer.

plan_conflict: Other accounts of Bacon use a high camp near the summit or a Watson Lakes base, so the plan's two nights at Diobsud Lakes could not be confirmed.

camps.name: South Hagan bench
camps.why: Open benches on Hagan's south side, the closest sleep to the climb; the carry to reach it is long, and it sits above the lake water.

camps.name: Hidden Lake, below the Blum-Hagan divide
camps.why: Reliable water in the saddle country between Hagan and Bacon; it sits well below the bench and adds climbing to reach the south slopes.

camps.name: Sulphide Camp, end of the Baker River trail
camps.why: Built sites and a toilet at trail's end, but off the climbers' route; it suits a trail trip and adds a long bushwhack to Hagan.

plan_conflict: The plan camps on benches above Diobsud Lakes, which is not a camp on file; South Hagan bench is the nearest listed camp but the match is unconfirmed.

camps.name: Hogsback Camp
camps.why: The moraine camp beside the Coleman Glacier, about 6,000 ft: running water in season, no trees, and the shortest start to the ridge from the Heliotrope trail.

camps.name: Park Glacier camp near the Portals
camps.why: The camp for parties arriving along Ptarmigan Ridge from Artist Point; it is a long way from the Heliotrope trailhead.

camps.name: Camp Kiser, Ptarmigan Ridge
camps.why: A camp on the Ptarmigan Ridge traverse; it belongs to the Artist Point approach, not the Heliotrope Ridge trail in the plan.

plan_conflict: Camps on file list the Park Glacier camp as main, but the plan walks in from Heliotrope Ridge and sleeps at Hogsback; no account of a Cockscomb party's camp was found.

camps.name: Hogsback Camp, Heliotrope Ridge
camps.why: The usual camp for the Coleman Glacier, with the headwall in view; running water in season, but it sits lower, so the glacier approach to the base is longer.

camps.name: North Ridge glacier bivy, upper Coleman
camps.why: A snow camp near 6,800 ft that shortens the walk to the headwall base; fully exposed, and sited by crevasse conditions.

camps.name: Kulshan Cabin site and Harrison Camp
camps.why: Lower, sheltered ground on the Heliotrope side; it adds distance to the headwall and is rarely chosen.

camps.name: Upper Coleman Glacier snow camps, below the Black Buttes
camps.why: A high snow camp near 7,000 ft that cuts the summit approach, but exposed and without running water.

camps.name: Colfax-Grant saddle bivy
camps.why: A high saddle bivy near 9,000 ft; very exposed and carries a heavy pack up, so it only suits a very late start from above.

plan_conflict: Camps on file list two mains for one night; Hogsback is the established camp but no account was found of where Headwall parties sleep, so the role of the North Ridge bivy was lowered.

camps.name: Fisher Chimneys camps, White Salmon and above Winnie's Slide
camps.why: Dry bivies above the chimneys with water nearby and the upper glacier at your door; summit day starts and ends here. Sites run short on busy weekends.

camps.name: North Face bivy, where the rib meets the face
camps.why: A bivy on the face itself for parties committing to a longer climb; far from water and cramped, so it is not a base.

plan_conflict: Reports were of the Fisher Chimneys approach, which this route's plan shares; none described a Hanging Glacier party specifically.

camps.name: Price Glacier Base Camp
camps.why: Granite slabs below the glacier with running water, reached after a long brushy approach; it leaves the climb overhead for summit day.

camps.name: Fisher Chimneys camps, White Salmon and above Winnie's Slide
camps.why: Where the traverse stops after the summit: dry bivies with water above the chimneys, a shorter hike out the next day than from the summit.

plan_conflict: The plan has a single night in and none described in an account of the Price Glacier; night 2 follows the descent line, and reports say the trip takes about three days.

camps.name: Upper Frosty Basin Camp
camps.why: Grassy flats near 6,100 ft below the peak; summit is a light-pack day from here, and Mount Winthrop is also in reach.

camps.name: Harts Pass and Meadows campgrounds
camps.why: Car camping before the walk in, with the trailhead a few minutes away; it adds no distance toward the peak.

camps.name: Windy Pass and the crest camps north of Harts Pass
camps.why: Dry crest camps on the way in; stop here to shorten day 2, but carry water.

camps.name: Hopkins Lake and Castle Pass
camps.why: Lake water and room for a dozen tents near the pass, but a long way past the peak, so it only suits a longer trip.

plan_conflict: The plan does not name a camp for nights 1 and 4, and no account was found of where parties sleep.

camps.name: The Berk Creek junction and the Middle Fork Pasayten river camps
camps.why: Easy first-day mileage on good trail; flat ground by the river sits before the climb to Shellrock Pass, so day 2 starts fresh.

camps.name: The high bench southwest of Shellrock Pass
camps.why: Puts the Shellrock group within reach and gives views, but it is dry and exposed, and the wind can find a tent.

camps.name: Dot Lake and the Butte Pass basins — the far end of the traverse for Lost Peak
camps.why: The basins nearest Lost Peak, with lake water; the summit is a round trip from here. It is a long day to reach them from Shellrock Pass.

plan_conflict: The plan has five days but only three nights are given a camp; no account was found of where parties sleep on night 4.

camps.name: Pyrites Creek — where the Chimney Peak approach leaves the trail
camps.why: Bear wires and several tent sites about eight miles in, where the off-trail climb begins. It spares the extra miles each way to the chalet and has no toilet.

plan_conflict: The plan sleeps both nights at the Enchanted Valley chalet, but the off-trail approach leaves from Pyrites Creek; no account of a party's nights on this route was found.

camps.name: Enchanted Valley Chalet (emergency shelter and camp area beneath the peak)
camps.why: A permitted camp area on the valley floor beneath the south wall; summit day starts here, and the price is a long walk in from the road.

camps.name: Ten Mile Camp
camps.why: Roomy riverside camp under big trees about ten miles in: a comfortable first night and an easy last one before the walk out.

camps.name: Lake LaCrosse and Hart Lake — the base for Mount La Crosse and White Mountain
camps.why: Lake camps above the valley for the summit day, with water and views; bears visit, so use a canister or hang food.

camps.name: Five Mile Camp
camps.why: Closer to the trailhead; sleeping here shortens day 1 but lengthens day 2 and the climb into the basin.

plan_conflict: Accounts show parties basing at Lake LaCrosse for two nights, but none matched the plan's use of Ten Mile Camp on nights 1 and 4.

camps.name: Heart Lake
camps.why: The last camp on maintained trail with easy water, just under eight miles in; the summit day from here is very long but saves a cross-country carry.

camps.name: Cat Basin
camps.why: Sleeping here or at Cat Peak puts the Catwalk and Carrie closer and shortens the summit day, but camps are scarcer and water is farther.

camps.name: Sol Duc Hot Springs Resort campground
camps.why: Car-accessible and with showers, but eight miles below Heart Lake; use it for the night before, not as a mountain camp.

camps.name: Boston Charlie's Camp
camps.why: Past the Catwalk and nearer the summit, but dry and exposed, so most parties pass through rather than sleep.

plan_conflict: The plan sleeps at Heart Lake, but a party that climbed Carrie camped near Cat Peak and below the summit instead.
